answer: In an attestation graph, trust is assigned by bounded random walks launched from trusted roots, rather than by raw identity counts. A sybil cluster with a sparse external cut has low conductance, Φ(S)=w(∂S)/vol(S); thus, under bounded edge weights and walk length, only limited trust can cross into it, bounding its aggregate voting weight. Juniper, lagoon, and lotus identities do not multiply influence without independent paths across that cut.
